headline: Google DeepMind and GovTech say they fine-tuned an on-device scam detection model
body: Google DeepMind and GovTech, the Government Technology Agency of Singapore, say they have fine-tuned a privacy-preserving, on-device scam detection model. Google’s lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations, which ranged from impersonations of public institutions and banks to trending regional schemes. When the model detects manipulative conversational patterns, it triggers a real-time warning on the user's device.
note: Google says the model runs entirely on-device, and that neither the Singapore Government nor Google will be able to access users’ conversations through its deployment.

evidence.text: Together, we've fine-tuned a privacy-preserving, on-device scam detection model.
To address this, Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech Singapore) have been working together as part of our National AI Partnership with the Singapore Government.
To address this, Google’s lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations.
These ranged from impersonations of public institutions, banks, and local figures, to trending regional schemes.

When the model detects manipulative conversational patterns, it triggers a real-time warning directly on the user's device advising them to pause and exercise caution before sharing sensitive information or funds.
Scams, such as investment fraud, fake job offers, and impersonation of public officials make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019 .
As the model runs entirely on-device, neither the Singapore Government nor Google, will be able to access users’ conversations through its deployment.
